findings.claim: The missing-kmctl hint tells the user to run `kmctl plugin install`, a verb this release does not have (it lands in plugin-install-verb). This breaks the rule skills-name-only-shipped-verbs in .claude/rules/cli-version-floor.md, and a user who follows the hint gets "No such command".

test_plugin_has_one_sessionstart_hook reads only plugin/hooks/hooks.json. A hooks field added to plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, or a second hooks file it points at, would add a hook and the test would still pass.

The hook sets no timeout, so a hung `kmctl briefing` holds session start for Claude Code's default hook timeout. A short `timeout` on the hook entry would keep I1's "never blocks" true in that case too.

verdict.text: The plugin, marketplace and hook do what the plan asks.
One SessionStart hook relays `kmctl briefing` and always exits 0.
The marketplace entry declares okf@scaccogatto and allowlists scaccogatto, as ADR 0003 says.
`claude plugin validate` accepts both manifests.
The one real defect is that the install hint names `kmctl plugin install`, which does not exist yet.
Dropping that clause fixes it, so it does not need another round.
The other two findings ask for a stronger test and a hook timeout.
The staged change in the worktree (it is staged, not committed): every file read in full.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass, eval rows r1 to r4 pass, "stamp green: d60c1b0b...".
I ran `claude plugin validate plugin` and `claude plugin validate .` myself (Claude Code 2.1.300).
Both pass.
r1: the test checks that the only event is SessionStart, that there is exactly one entry and one hook (through the list unpacking in `_hook_command`), and that the command contains `kmctl briefing`.
This matches fails_when, with the gap noted in f2.
r2: the test runs the real command under /bin/sh with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and checks exit 0 and the "uv tool install" hint.
If kmctl were in /usr/bin, the hint check would fail rather than pass by mistake.
r3: the test asserts the exact dependency object, the allowlist and the source.
r4: the test is real, but it skips when no claude CLI is on PATH, so CI without claude does not check it.
It ran here.
Consistency: I1 is enforced by the plugin tests and I3 by tests/test_briefing.py::test_briefing_word_budget, which exists and asserts the budget.
Both meet the manifesto-invariants rule.
ADR 0003 and ADR 0004 match the change.
`kmctl --help` shows no `plugin` command.
f1: the hint text in hooks.json names `kmctl plugin install`.
That verb is not shipped (see `kmctl --help`), and the cli-version-floor rule forbids the hook naming verbs that are not shipped.
It is non-blocking because the fix is to delete one clause, or to add it back in plugin-install-verb along with the verb.
f2: the one-hook check looks only at hooks.json.
It is non-blocking because asserting that plugin.json has no `hooks` key is a one-line addition.
f3: there is no hook timeout.
It is non-blocking hardening, because the default timeout still ends the hook.
